D001-D013_h001.question:
It’s been about four months now that I just haven’t been myself. Since my husband passed a few years ago I’ve had ups and downs, but these last months it feels like I’ve sunk into a hole I can’t climb out of. I wake up heavy, dreading the day, and I don’t enjoy my volunteer work at the church like I used to. Most days I’m just sad or numb, and it’s hard to see the point of anything.

During this time my mind feels foggy. I can’t concentrate on simple things—sorting donation lists, planning events, even following a TV show. I lose track of what I’m doing and get pulled off by random thoughts about my husband or worries about the future. I never had these focus problems before I started feeling this low.

I used to be very organized with my projects, but lately I can’t keep tasks straight, and it frustrates me. I pace around the house a lot because I’m too agitated to sit and read, and when I’m with others I sometimes ramble on more than I mean to, just to fill the silence and distract myself from how empty I feel.

    B. Major Depressive Disorder
    C. Specific Phobia
    D. Schizophrenia
